pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/kit/FloorKit.tsx:52 The Floor specimen restates the readiness command as a third hand-typed copy (lines 52-53), while the named authority PUBLISH_CLI in app/(studio)/floor/_calendar/readiness.ts:33 is imported by both the real side and fixture.ts:33/241; nothing checks the kit copy, so if the CLI changes, /kit keeps showing the old command.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/kit/FloorKit.tsx:52 A literal copy of a fact that already has a named authority (PUBLISH_CLI, whose comment says 'the fixture side names the same'). The technique says a literal copy is asserted mechanically or derived. This one is neither: rg found no test comparing the kit copy to PUBLISH_CLI.

app/(studio)/kit/BoardKit.tsx:84 Each screen card declares which @gt/ui exports it draws (data-specimen). Coverage is then gated by walking the package's exports, not by checking only the names the map lists (tests/live/kit.live.spec.ts:24-58).
app/(studio)/kit/LibraryKit.tsx:86 The rail and the set summary read one object, matching the live screen. Before the fix the kit handed them two objects that disagreed (kit-sheet.test.ts case 9).

app/(studio)/kit/FloorKit.tsx:54 The commands shown can be pasted, but none takes a credential as a positional argument and none is an install line. The technique's two populations are absent; the drift risk falls under named-duplication-points.
